gap: No result ChatGPT got states that at today's maker-store prices the 45 W chargers under $20 cost about a third less per watt than ChatGPT's pick: UGREEN Nexode Air 45W $15.19 ÷ 45 W = $0.34/W and Anker Nano Charger Neo $15.99 ÷ 45 W sustained = $0.36/W, against the Anker Nano 30W at $15.99 ÷ 30 W = $0.53/W, or $0.59 per watt at the 27 W PPS that Android Authority measured.
standout_why: TechGearLab's Anker Nano 30W review (cited) prints a $16 list price and 29.4 W measured, but no cost per watt and no 45 W option under $20. Its comparison set is all 20 W chargers. Android Authority (cited) gives the Nano 3 30W a $22.99 MSRP and 27 W PPS but no per-watt figure, and it does not list the UGREEN Nexode Air 45W or the Anker Nano Charger Neo. For Tom's Hardware's best-USB-chargers page (cited), WebFetch returned only the navigation, so I could not check its body. It may print prices, but no snippet suggested a per-watt comparison. The arithmetic is simple, so the value is in the inputs: today's prices put 45 W units at the same money as the 30 W pick.
decides: ChatGPT's $15.99 Anker Nano 30W tier is no longer the most watts under $20. For the same $15.99, or $0.80 less, a shopper gets 45 W from one port, which is 1.5× the watts. That argues for ranking a 45 W charger first on decision factor 1 (most watts one port gives one device). It does not settle the pick by itself, for three reasons. Both 45 W units are under $20 only at sale prices (compare-at $24.99 and $25.99). Their 45 W figures are maker ratings with no named lab test I could open. And the Neo's AVS claim is unconfirmed: in the MacBook test The Gadgeteer cites, it negotiated USB PD 3.0 rather than AVS. The UGREEN Nexode Air 45W is a cj:ugreen partner product with no record yet. It belongs in this table on the question's own terms and can be added at https://us.ugreen.com/products/nexode-air-usb-c-charger-45w-gan-foldable-plug, $15.19 read 2026-11-27.
